question.text:
A processor has the following memory system characteristics:

  • Main memory access time $=100 \mathrm{~ns}$
     
  • Cache access time $=5 \mathrm{~ns}$
     
  • Cache is write-back, write-allocate, block size = 16 bytes
     
  • Cache read miss rate $=4 \%$, write miss rate $=20 \%$
     
  • On a write miss, the entire block is loaded from memory before updating the cache
     
  • On a write hit, the block is updated in cache only
     
  • $20 \%$ of the cache blocks are dirty when they are replaced
     
  • Assume $30 \%$ of all memory accesses are writes

The average memory access time (AMAT) for this system (in ns) is __________.
question.subject: CO & Architecture

question.text:
A scalar in-order processor has a base CPI of $1$ in the absence of control hazards. The instruction mix of a program is such that conditional branches are $20$ percent of all instructions and unconditional branches are $5$ percent. The branch target buffer has a hit rate of $80$ percent for both branch types. For conditional branches, when the BTB hits, a $2$-bit saturating counter predictor is used whose direction accuracy is $92$ percent. Unconditional branches are always taken. The actual taken probability of conditional branches is $60$ percent. A direction misprediction incurs a penalty of $5$ cycles. When a branch is taken but the BTB misses, there is a $2$-cycle target resolution penalty even if the direction would have been correct; when a conditional branch is not taken and the BTB misses, there is no penalty. Assume no overlap between penalties and ignore all other stalls.

The average CPI of this processor is _______ (up to $3$ decimal places)

question.text:
Consider the standard pipelined execution of the following instruction sequence:

I1: MUL R1, R2, R3

I2: ADD R4, R1, R5

I3: SUB R6, R4, R7

  • Initially, registers contain: $\mathrm{R} 2=3, \mathrm{R} 3=5, \mathrm{R} 5=2, \mathrm{R} 7=4$.
     
  • The processor uses forwarding from the ALU output to the input of subsequent ALU operations.
     
  • Instructions are fetched one per cycle, starting from cycle 1.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

A. There is a RAW dependency between I1 and I2.

B. After execution of the sequence, the content of the registers is $R 1=-2, R 4=-7, R 6=-11 $

C. 8 stalls are created due to RAW hazard

D. A structural hazard will occur due to the ALU being used by multiple instructions.
question.subject: CO & Architecture

question.text:
Assume that the following instruction sequence is executed on standard pipeline:

$$
\begin{aligned}
& 11: R 1=R 2+R 3 \\
& 12: R 4=R 1+R 5 \\
& 13: R 1=R 6-R 7 \\
& 14: R 5=R 1+R 8 \\
& 15: R 6=R 4+R 1
\end{aligned}
$$


Which of the following statements is/are not true?

  1. There are 3 RAW dependencies in this sequence
     
  2. There are 3 WAR hazards in this sequence
     
  3. There are 1 WAW hazard in this sequence
     
  4. There is a RAW hazard between I1 and I4
question.subject: CO & Architecture

question.text:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding the single-issue pipeline?

  1. True data dependency always creates stalls in the pipeline
     
  2. WAR/WAW hazards may or may not be there in the pipeline
     
  3. Out-of-order execution can eliminate some stalls caused by true data dependencies.
     
  4. Structural dependency may or may not create stalls if no additional hardware is used.
